'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[German support for Israel in the Gaza war]], [[Germany–Israel relations]]
***[[Germany]] expects to lift its restrictions on [[military technology|military equipment]] exports to [[Israel]] from November 24, which were banned in August due to the [[siege of Gaza City]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-israel-military-export-restrictions-5dc988d1472099db3f06a2c3232b7f78 (AP)]
**[[Gaza peace plan]]
***The [[United Nations Security Council]] votes in favor of a [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803|US-drafted resolution]] endorsing the peace plan, including the establishment of the [[International Stabilization Force]] (ISF) and [[Board of Peace]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c0rpkgq4wllo (BBC News)]
*[[Russo-Ukrainian war (2022–present)|Russo-Ukrainian war]]
**[[Kharkiv strikes (2022–present)|Kharkiv strikes]]
***A [[Russia]]n missile strike on a residential area in [[Balakliia]], [[Kharkiv Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], kills three people and injures 10 others. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/three-killed-10-wounded-russian-missile-strike-kharkiv-region-ukraine-says-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
**[[Military aid to Ukraine during the Russo-Ukrainian war]], [[France–Ukraine relations]]
***[[Ukraine]] signs an agreement with [[France]] to receive up to 100 [[Dassault Rafale|Rafale]] [[Fighter aircraft|fighter jets]], along with [[anti-aircraft warfare]], munitions, and [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drones]]. Both governments say the proposed use of [[Confiscation of Russian central bank funds|frozen Russian assets]] will partly finance it. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/17/europe/ukraine-buys-french-fighter-jets-intl (CNN)]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**In [[Lahij]], [[Yemen]], suspected [[Houthis|Houthi]] gunmen carry out an [[ambush]] against a convoy carrying the governor of [[Taiz Governorate|Taiz]] and a military commander, killing five of their bodyguards. Both the governor and the commander are unharmed, while two gunmen are also killed. [https://english.news.cn/20251125/63a654edc97246d3919f705f61d09e37/c.html (Xinhua)]
*[[Druze insurgency in Southern Syria (2025–present)|Druze insurgency in Southern Syria]]
**An investigative committee in [[Syria]] detains members of the country's [[Syrian Armed Forces|military]] and [[Desert Security Forces (Syria)|security forces]] in an investigation into [[sectarian violence]] in [[Sweida]] in July involving the [[Druze in Syria|Druze]]. [https://apnews.com/article/syria-sweida-druze-violence-sectarian-killings-10ee66c7fcb33b7291b137a2bdbeb57b (AP)]
*[[Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa]]
**Thirty-eight [[Pakistani Taliban]] militants are killed by the [[Pakistan Army|army]] in a series of raids since yesterday in [[Dera Ismail Khan]], [[North Waziristan District|North Waziristan]], [[Bannu]] and [[Bajaur District|Bajaur]], in [[Pakistan]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-security-raids-militants-killed-northwest-4afd66f63cc825fa34902f228659b971 (AP)]
*[[Nigerian bandit conflict]], [[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**Gunmen kidnap 25 female students from and kill the vice principal of a [[secondary school]] in Maga, [[Kebbi State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/nigeria-gunmen-kidnap-25-students-from-kebbi-high-school/a-74782165 (DW)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5ypn7pwgv5o (BBC News)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[Cambridge University Press and Assessment]] announces ''[[parasocial]]'' as its [[word of the year]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2025/11/17/world/parasocial-cambridge-dictionary-scli-intl (CNN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Spain|Spanish]] [[Ministry of Development (Spain)|transport minister]] [[Óscar Puente]] announces the [[AVE|AV350]] project, which will upgrade the [[Madrid–Barcelona high-speed rail line]] to a maximum operating speed of {{cvt|350|km/h|mph}} and make it one of [[List of speed records in rail transport|the world's fastest trains]]. Puente says work is scheduled to begin next year and is expected to take three years. [https://www.reuters.com/business/spain-aims-cut-madrid-barcelona-high-speed-rail-time-under-two-hours-minister-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
*At the [[Dubai Airshow]], [[United Arab Emirates|UAE]] [[Flag carrier|flagship airline]] [[Emirates (airline)|Emirates]] announces a deal to buy 65 [[Boeing]] [[Boeing 777-9|777-9]] aircraft worth [[US$]]38 billion, with deliveries starting in 2027. [https://apnews.com/article/dubai-air-show-boeing-airbus-emirates-flydubai-ca30a6ba8d90dee5b2cf4ba1c3fd43db (AP)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2025 Medina bus crash]]
**A bus carrying [[Indian people|Indian]] [[Umrah]] [[Pilgrimage|pilgrims]] collides with a [[tank truck]] near [[Medina]], [[Saudi Arabia]], killing 45 people. [https://www.msn.com/en-in/news/india/42-indian-pilgrims-feared-dead-in-bus-tanker-collision-near-medina-in-saudi-arabia/ar-AA1Qz0Sv?ocid=msedgntp&pc=U531&cvid=5f440525dbad46fbb32bfdc27c50e374&ei=14 (''Hindustan Times'')]
*The toll from yesterday's bus crash in Simiatug, [[Tungurahua Province]], [[Ecuador]], increases to 21 people killed and 40 others injured. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/death-toll-ecuador-bus-crash-climbs-21-40-injured-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
*Six people are killed and 19 others are injured when a [[landslide]] triggered by heavy rain strikes a bus carrying 32 passengers in [[Khánh Vĩnh district]], [[Khánh Hòa province]], [[Vietnam]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/landslide-kills-6-bus-passengers-central-vietnam-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
*Five [[Tourism in Chile|tourists]] are killed in a [[blizzard]] in [[Torres del Paine National Park]] in [[Chile]]an [[Patagonia]], where [[Chilean Armed Forces|military]] and [[Carabineros de Chile|police]] rescue four others and continue [[search and rescue]] operations. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20251118-two-mexicans-killed-seven-visitors-missing-in-chilean-patagonia-blizzard-officials (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Airjet Angola Flight MBC-100]]
**An [[Embraer ERJ-145]] operating as [[Airjet Exploração Aérea de Carga|AirJet Angola]] Flight 100 carrying 29 members of a {{ill|Ministry of Mines (Democratic Republic of the Congo)|fr|Ministère des Mines (république démocratique du Congo)|lt=Ministry of Mines}} delegation crashes while attempting to land at [[Kolwezi Airport]] in [[Lualaba Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. No casualties are reported. [https://aviation-safety.net/wikibase/561999 (ASN)] [https://www.israelhayom.com/2025/11/17/congo-plane-crash-mining-minister-louis-watom-kabamba-survives-kolwezi/ (''Israel Hayom'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[Polio eradication]], [[Health in Pakistan]]
**[[Polio in Pakistan]]
***[[Pakistan]] launches an initiative to vaccinate 34.5 million children against [[measles]] and [[rubella]] and 23.3 million against [[polio]]. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-launched-drive-measles-polio-rubella-bd04a22bb5ed53949cbc53978b956925 (AP)]
*[[Health in Ethiopia]]
**[[Ethiopia]] confirms three deaths from a [[Marburg virus disease]] declared on Friday in [[West Omo Zone]]. [https://www.euronews.com/health/2025/11/17/ethiopia-confirms-3-deaths-from-ebola-like-marburg-virus-in-new-outbreak (Euronews)]
*At least 71 schools in [[Australia]] and [[New Zealand]] close as authorities investigate [[Product recall|recalled]] children's [[Hydrophobic sand|play sand]] products from [[Kmart Australia|Kmart]] and [[Target Australia|Target]] after testing detected [[asbestos]] in some samples. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/asbestos-contamination-forces-schools-australia-new-zealand-close-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Nicaragua–United States relations]], [[Immigration policy of the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States]] imposes [[Visa policy of the United States|visa restrictions]] and revokes some existing visas for [[Nicaraguans]], including owners of [[Transport in Nicaragua|transportation]] and [[Travel agency|travel companies]], who it says facilitate [[Illegal immigration to the United States|illegal immigration to the U.S.]] under [[Nicaragua]]'s migration policies. [https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/us-imposes-visa-restrictions-nicaragua-over-immigration-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Capital punishment in Bangladesh]], [[Trial of Sheikh Hasina]]
**A [[International Crimes Tribunal (Bangladesh)|domestic tribunal]] in [[Bangladesh]] sentences former [[Prime Minister of Bangladesh|prime minister]] [[Sheikh Hasina]] and former home minister [[Asaduzzaman Khan]] to death [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]] over [[crimes against humanity]] committed during the [[2024 Bangladesh quota reform movement|quota reform protests]] in 2024. [https://apnews.com/article/bangladesh-hasina-verdict-yunus-security-c1eec828e68460bae66824601a94eaca (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/bangladeshs-ousted-pm-hasina-convicted-students-crackdown-case-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 Chilean presidential election]]
**Due to no candidates receiving 50% of the vote in the [[President of Chile|presidential]] election, a [[run-off election|runoff]] occurs between [[Communist Party of Chile|left-wing]] candidate [[Jeannette Jara]] of the [[Unidad por Chile|Unity for Chile]] coalition and [[Republican Party of Chile|right-wing]] candidate [[José Antonio Kast]] of the [[Change for Chile]] coalition, with the vote set for December 14. [https://www.dw.com/en/chile-far-left-far-right-candidates-proceed-to-runoff-vote/a-74770287 (DW)]
*[[2025 Iraqi parliamentary election]]
**The [[Independent High Electoral Commission]] releases the seat distribution from [[Iraq]]'s recent election as [[Prime Minister of Iraq|prime minister]] [[Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani]]'s [[2021–2022 Iraqi political crisis|Coordination Framework]] alliance declares that it will form the [[Majority government|majority]] bloc and will nominate the next prime minister. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iraqi-pm-led-coalition-tops-iraq-election-with-46-seats-commission-says-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Flood control projects controversy in the Philippines]]
**[[Philippines|Philippine]] [[Executive Secretary (Philippines)|executive secretary]] [[Lucas Bersamin]] and [[Secretary of Budget and Management|budget secretary]] [[Amenah Pangandaman]] resign over their alleged involvement in [[flood control]] [[Corruption in the Philippines|corruption]]. [[Secretary of Finance (Philippines)|Finance secretary]] [[Ralph Recto]] replaces Bersamin as the executive secretary. [https://gulfnews.com/world/asia/philippines/philippines-2-marcos-cabinet-members-resign-over-ghost-flood-control-projects-1.500349110 (''Gulf News'')]
*[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia]]
**[[Russia]]'s [[Rosfinmonitoring]] adds former [[Prime Minister of Russia|prime minister]] [[Mikhail Kasyanov]] and [[London Business School]] dean [[Sergei Guriev]] to [[List of organizations designated as terrorist or extremist by Russia|its list of extremists and terrorists]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/russia-adds-ex-pm-kasyanov-economist-guriev-extremists-terrorists-list-2025-11-17/ (Reuters)]
